iterations.theme: Što je uspjeh za muškarca: slike iz djetinjstva, očekivanja, uspoređivanje i novac kao mjerilo vlastite vrijednosti

sections.subtitle: Muške glave za istim stolom: moramo li uopće uspjeti?
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Marko otvara epizodu i najavljuje temu muškog uspjeha pred dvojicom gostiju
sections.content:
Novu epizodu EHOCAST-a, podcasta Molitvene zajednice Eho, voditelj **Marko** otvara pozdravom „Hvaljen Isus i Marija“ i najavom drugačijeg formata. Nakon nekoliko razgovora jedan na jedan, ovoga se puta, kako sam kaže, okupilo više „muških glava“ koje će pokušati „donijeti neku mudrost“. Prva tema postavljena je izravno: **moramo li uspjeti i što za muškarca uopće znači uspjeh?**

Marko predstavlja goste. Jedan je **Fran**, član zajednice, a drugi vanjski suradnik **Mislav**, kojega publika na društvenim mrežama poznaje kao **Tatu Hrasta**. Cilj razgovora, objašnjava voditelj, jest podijeliti osobna iskustva u kojima bi se slušatelji mogli prepoznati. Dodaje i da bi nešto mogli naučiti i sami sudionici. U šaljivom tonu najavljuje da bi netko nakon razgovora mogao donijeti velike odluke i „otvoriti neke firme ili obrte“, pa čak i obiteljsko gospodarstvo.

Atmosfera je od prvih minuta opuštena. Marko se šali da je on „kao domaćin“, a Fran mu odgovara da je on „kao gost“.
sections.subtitle_en: Men's Heads at the Same Table: Do We Even Have to Succeed?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Marko opens the episode and announces the theme of male success before two guests
sections.content_en:
The host **Marko** opens the new episode of EHOCAST, the podcast of the Eho Prayer Community, with the greeting "Praise be Jesus and Mary" and the announcement of a different format. After several one-on-one conversations, this time, as he says himself, several "men's heads" have gathered who will try to "bring some wisdom." The first topic was posed directly: **do we have to succeed and what does success even mean for a man?**

Marko introduces the guests. One is **Fran**, a member of the community, and the other is an external collaborator **Mislav**, whom the audience on social media knows as **Tata Hrast**. The goal of the conversation, the host explains, is to share personal experiences in which the listeners could recognize themselves. He also adds that the participants themselves could learn something. In a humorous tone, he announces that after the conversation someone might make big decisions and "open some companies or trades," and even a family farm.

The atmosphere is relaxed from the very first minutes. Marko jokes that he is "like a host," and Fran responds to him that he is "like a guest."

sections.subtitle: Fran: od nagovora prijateljice do slavljeničkog tima
sections.screenshot_description: Fran priča kako je došao u zajednicu
sections.content:
Marko prednost u predstavljanju daje Franu kao članu zajednice, kako bi ga gledatelji bolje upoznali. Fran se našalio da je na snimanje došao samo zato što ga je voditelj „natjerao“. Zatim objašnjava da je u zajednicu stigao **na nagovor prijateljice Vinke**, koju pozdravlja, i da mu se od tada „život okrenuo“.

Na prvi susret došao je **2020. godine**, a članom zajednice postao je već **2021.** Uz osmijeh dodaje da mu „nije dugo trebalo da se pokaže u dobrom svjetlu“. Danas je dio **slavljeničkog tima** i pomaže u raznim zadacima. Za Marka kaže da mu je postao vrlo dobar prijatelj, pa zaključuje da je u podcast „došao preko veze“.
sections.subtitle_en: Fran: From a Female Friend's Persuasion to the Worship Team
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran talks about how he came to the community
sections.content_en:
Marko gives priority in the introduction to Fran as a member of the community, so that the viewers could get to know him better. Fran joked that he came to the recording only because the host "forced" him. Then he explains that he arrived in the community **at the persuasion of his friend Vinka**, whom he greets, and that since then his "life turned around."

He came to the first meeting in **2020**, and became a member of the community already in **2021**. With a smile, he adds that "it didn't take him long to show himself in a good light." Today he is part of the **worship team** and helps in various tasks. Regarding Marko, he says that he has become a very good friend to him, so he concludes that he came to the podcast "through connections."

sections.subtitle: Mislav – Tata Hrast: „veza odozgo“ i životni zaokret
sections.screenshot_description: Mislav, poznat kao Tata Hrast, objašnjava kako je upoznao voditelja
sections.content:
Marko otkriva da se s Mislavom dotad čuo tek usputno. Ipak, svidio mu se njegov način razmišljanja i način na koji funkcionira u novom životu koji je pokrenuo. Mislav nadovezuje na Franovu šalu: i on je došao „preko veze“, ali **„preko ove gore veze“**, jer vjeruje da je neka veza morala postojati da se njih dvojica spoje.

Upoznali su se preko društvenih mreža, gdje su razmijenili nekoliko komentara, „par pametnih, par duhovnih“. Mislavu se svidjelo ono što Marko govori i način na koji zajednica djeluje. To se, kaže, snažno poklapa s njegovim načinom života u posljednjih nekoliko godina, otkako su on i njegova obitelj napravili **presjek i zaokret, i privatno i poslovno**.

Markovu šalu o otvaranju firmi Mislav duhovito okreće: možda će netko nakon ovog razgovora firmu i zatvoriti. Fran dobacuje: „Stavi ključ u bravu.“
sections.subtitle_en: Mislav – Tata Hrast: "Connection from Above" and a Life Pivot
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mislav, known as Tata Hrast, explains how he met the host
sections.content_en:
Marko reveals that he had only casually been in touch with Mislav until then. Still, he liked his way of thinking and the way he functions in the new life he started. Mislav builds on Fran's joke: he also came "through connections," but **"through this connection up above,"** because he believes that some connection had to exist for the two of them to connect.

They met via social media, where they exchanged several comments, "a couple smart ones, a couple spiritual ones." Mislav liked what Marko speaks and the way the community operates. That, he says, strongly coincides with his way of life over the last few years, since he and his family made **a clean break and a pivot, both privately and in business**.

Mislav humorously turns Marko's joke about opening companies around: perhaps someone will even close a company after this conversation. Fran chimes in: "Put the key in the lock."

sections.subtitle: Dvostruka mjerila: neuredan stan za nju, prazan novčanik za njega
sections.screenshot_description: Marko opisuje razliku u društvenim očekivanjima od muškaraca i žena
sections.content:
Prije ulaska u osobne priče Marko postavlja okvir. Predrasude i očekivanja postoje prema ženama, ali i prema muškarcima. Ilustrira to situacijom iz vlastitog braka. Supruga je jednom bila pod stresom jer stan nije bio uredan, svjesna da se od nje u tome očekuje mnogo više. Marko joj je potvrdio da je u pravu: nitko neće ući u stan i pomisliti da Marko nije pospremio za sobom.

Dodao je, međutim, i drugu stranu medalje. **Ako obitelji zaškripi financijski, nitko neće pitati zašto Mirjana nije više radila, nego zašto se on nije pobrinuo, zašto to nije riješio.** Marko naglašava da to vrijedi bez obzira na to što supruga ravnopravno sudjeluje u radu i poslu, ima vlastitu firmu i bavi se javnim nastupom. Očekivanja na tom području, zaključuje, jednostavno su drugačija.
sections.subtitle_en: Double Standards: A Messy Apartment for Her, an Empty Wallet for Him
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko describes the difference in societal expectations of men and women
sections.content_en:
Before entering into personal stories, Marko sets the framework. Prejudices and expectations exist toward women, but also toward men. He illustrates this with a situation from his own marriage. His wife was once under stress because the apartment was not tidy, conscious that much more is expected of her in that regard. Marko confirmed to her that she was right: nobody will walk into the apartment and think that Marko did not clean up after himself.

He added, however, the other side of the coin as well. **If things get tight financially for the family, nobody will ask why Mirjana didn't work more, but why he didn't take care of it, why he didn't solve it.** Marko emphasizes that this holds true regardless of the fact that his wife participates equally in work and business, has her own company, and engages in public speaking. Expectations in that area, he concludes, are simply different.

sections.subtitle: Mislav: neuspjeh je imao zvuk obiteljskih svađa oko novca
sections.screenshot_description: Mislav govori o obiteljskim tenzijama iz djetinjstva vezanim uz novac
sections.content:
Marko pita kakav je u djetinjstvu bio njihov ideal uspješnog muškarca. Mislav odgovara da **nikada nije imao idole** i da od toga oduvijek bježi. Umjesto toga, pažljivo je „čitao“ odnose u obitelji i iz njih učio kakav muškarac želi biti, a kakav ne, te kakve odnose želi imati.

Upravo su iz tih odnosa nastale njegove slike uspjeha i neuspjeha. **Neuspjeh mu se povezivao s tenzijama i svađama u obitelji.** Takve situacije, ističe, utječu na djecu htjeli to roditelji ili ne, bez obzira na to misle li da su djeca dovoljno daleko ili u svojoj sobi. Gotovo svaki od tih problema bio je vezan uz novac. Mislav posebno naglašava da novca nije nedostajalo: **jednostavno bi „zaškripalo“**, pa se u nekom trenutku nije moglo napraviti ono što je trebalo. Majka i otac podjednako su sudjelovali u financijama kućanstva.

Tek kao odrasla osoba, kada je osnovao vlastitu obitelj, shvatio je ključnu stvar. Cijeli je život proveo u **„survival modu“, načinu preživljavanja**, u kojem je svoj uspjeh i vrijednost mjerio iznosom novca koji može zaraditi i kojim može pridonijeti obitelji.

Na Markovo potpitanje potvrđuje da se to razvilo s vremenom. Cilj mu je bio što prije početi raditi i privređivati, jer je tako znao da je siguran: najprije on sam, a kasnije i njegova obitelj. Bilo da je bio zaposlen kod nekoga kao „najbolji radnik ikad“ ili je „ginuo“ za vlastitu firmu i klijente, taj se obrazac prelio na ostatak života. **„Kako raste titula, kako rastu financije, tako rastu i apetiti“**, objašnjava. Za sebe kaže da je bio **„hiperambiciozan“** i da ambicija bez prave mjere može otići jako u krivo.
sections.subtitle_en: Mislav: Failure Had the Sound of Family Arguments Over Money
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mislav talks about family tensions from childhood related to money
sections.content_en:
Marko asks what their ideal of a successful man was in childhood. Mislav answers that **he never had idols** and that he has always run away from that. Instead, he carefully "read" the relationships in the family and learned from them what kind of man he wants to be, and what kind not, and what kind of relationships he wants to have.

It was precisely out of those relationships that his images of success and failure arose. **Failure was associated in his mind with tensions and arguments in the family.** Such situations, he points out, affect children whether parents want it or not, regardless of whether they think the children are far enough away or in their room. Almost every single one of those problems was related to money. Mislav particularly emphasizes that there was no lack of money: **things would simply "get tight,"** so at a certain moment what needed to be done could not be done. Mother and father participated equally in the household finances.

Only as an adult, when he established his own family, did he realize the key thing. He spent his entire life in **"survival mode," a way of surviving**, in which he measured his success and worth by the amount of money he can earn and with which he can contribute to the family.

To Marko's follow-up question, he confirms that this developed over time. His goal was to start working and earning as soon as possible, because that way he knew he was safe: first he himself, and later his family as well. Whether he was employed with someone as "the best worker ever" or was "dying" for his own company and clients, that pattern spilled over into the rest of his life. **"As the title grows, as finances grow, so do the appetites grow,"** he explains. About himself he says that he was **"hyper-ambitious"** and that ambition without a proper measure can go very wrong.

sections.subtitle: Fran: tetak iz Petrokemije, otac uvijek kod kuće i golmanski snovi
sections.screenshot_description: Fran se prisjeća oca ratnog invalida i tetka koji je radio u Petrokemiji
sections.content:
Fran svoju dječju sliku uspjeha dijeli na **dvije kategorije**. Prvu je utjelovljivao tetak, koji je „otkako zna za sebe“ radio u **Petrokemiji u Kutini**, kako je Fran opisuje, u „firmetini“ u kojoj svatko u kraju ima nekoga iz obitelji. Tetak je uvijek bio sređen, pazio je na detalje i bio je „baš gospodin“.

Drugu je kategoriju predstavljao njegov otac. Kao **ratni invalid**, s otprilike 28 ili 29 godina otišao je u ratnu mirovinu i od tada je bio stalno kod kuće s djecom. Igrao se s njima i uvijek je bio prisutan. Fran naglašava da je otac želio raditi, ali mu liječnici to zbog invalidnosti nisu dopuštali. Tako je **uspješan muškarac u poslovnom svijetu za njega bio tetak, a uspješan otac njegov „stari“**. „Stvarno je bilo predobro odrastati s tatom koji je stalno doma“, kaže Fran.

Njegov osobni dječji san bio je golmanski. Želio je postati zvijezda poput tadašnjeg vratara hrvatske reprezentacije, a uzor mu je bio i **Neuer**: „Ako ću uspjeti, moram braniti kao on.“ Marko u šali dobacuje ime Butina.

Kada je riječ o uspjehu u odrasloj dobi, Fran priznaje da mu je ta tema daleko od razmišljanja i da ne bi znao „staviti na papir“ što je uspjeh. Sebe zato opisuje kao **„drugu stranu medalje u ovom podcastu“**. Ostaje i poštapalica o Kutini: „Ako si u Petrokemiji, buraz, najbolji si.“
sections.subtitle_en: Fran: The Uncle from Petrokemija, a Father Always at Home, and Goalkeeping Dreams
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran recalls his father, a disabled war veteran, and his uncle who worked at Petrokemija
sections.content_en:
Fran divides his childhood image of success into **two categories**. The first was embodied by his uncle, who "for as long as he knows himself" worked at **Petrokemija in Kutina**, as Fran describes it, in a "huge company" where everyone in the region has someone from their family. The uncle was always well-groomed, paid attention to details, and was "truly a gentleman."

The second category was represented by his father. As a **disabled war veteran**, at about 28 or 29 years of age he went into a war disability pension and from then on was constantly at home with the children. He played with them and was always present. Fran emphasizes that his father wanted to work, but doctors did not allow him to do so because of his disability. Thus, **a successful man in the business world for him was his uncle, and a successful father his "old man."** "It was really too good growing up with a dad who is constantly at home," Fran says.

His personal childhood dream was goalkeeping. He wanted to become a star like the then-goalkeeper of the Croatian national team, and his role model was also **Neuer**: "If I'm going to succeed, I have to defend like him." Marko jokingly tosses in the name Butina.

When it comes to success in adulthood, Fran admits that that topic is far from his thoughts and that he wouldn't know how to "put on paper" what success is. He therefore describes himself as **"the other side of the coin in this podcast."** There also remains the catchphrase about Kutina: "If you're at Petrokemija, bro, you're the best."

sections.subtitle: Marko: BMW X5, odijela i san o menadžerstvu od četvrtog razreda
sections.screenshot_description: Marko se prisjeća dječjeg sna o korporaciji, odijelima i BMW-u
sections.content:
Za razliku od Frana, Marko točno zna što je kao dijete smatrao uspjehom. Već u **četvrtom razredu osnovne škole razmišljao je o korporaciji i menadžerstvu**. Prvih pet razreda išao je u razred sa sinom **pokojnog Stjepana Spajića**. Otac njegova školskog kolege vozio je BMW, imao telefon i uvijek je nosio odijelo kad je dolazio po sina ili ih vozio.

Od tada je **BMW X5** za Marka bio „najbolji auto“, a san se vrtio oko svijeta nogometnih menadžera, banaka, firmi i odijela. U tom razdoblju nije znao čime se taj čovjek bavi. Najdraža igrica bila mu je nogometni menadžer. Sve je to oblikovalo smjer kojim je namjeravao ići.

Čak i nakon obraćenja planirao je upisati ekonomiju, i to ne iz neodlučnosti, nego zato što je točno znao kamo ide. Ipak, kako kaže, Bog mu je „pomrsio planove“. Godinu dana ranije počeo je voditi mlade i shvatio da je to njegov put. Otac mu je imao prosječan posao i bio je vrijedan, ali ga Marko kao dijete nije doživljavao kao model uspjeha.

Od cijele dječje vizije, šali se Marko, ostali su mu tek sakoi koje je često nosio kad je počeo javno govoriti: „Nije banka, ali imam sakoe.“
sections.subtitle_en: Marko: BMW X5, Suits, and the Dream of Management Since the Fourth Grade
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko recalls a childhood dream of a corporation, suits, and a BMW
sections.content_en:
Unlike Fran, Marko knows exactly what he considered success as a child. Already in the **fourth grade of elementary school he thought about a corporation and management**. For the first five grades he went to class with the son of **the late Stjepan Spajić**. His classmate's father drove a BMW, had a phone, and always wore a suit when he came to pick up his son or drove them.

From then on, the **BMW X5** was "the best car" for Marko, and the dream revolved around the world of football managers, banks, companies, and suits. During that period he did not know what that man did for a living. His favorite game was football manager. All of that shaped the direction in which he intended to go.

Even after his conversion he planned to enroll in economics, and that not out of indecisiveness, but because he knew exactly where he was going. Still, as he says, God "disrupted his plans." A year earlier he had started leading youth and realized that this was his path. His father had an average job and was hardworking, but Marko as a child did not perceive him as a model of success.

From the entire childhood vision, Marko jokes, all that remained for him were the suit jackets that he often wore when he started speaking publicly: "It's not a bank, but I have the suit jackets."

sections.subtitle: Cilj za ciljem: kad posao proguta cijeli identitet
sections.screenshot_description: Mislav objašnjava kako je njegov identitet postao vezan uz posao
sections.content:
Marko zatim pita jesu li imali očekivanja o tome što moraju postići do tridesete. Fran se šali da su on i Marko još daleko od te dobi jer ima 25 godina. Mislav pak opisuje trenutak kada je ušao u **marketinšku industriju**. Tada je prvi put osjetio da je njegov uspjeh izravno vezan uz novac.

Od tada je započeo niz pitanja koja su ga stalno pratila:
- koliko mora biti sposoban,
- koliko i kome mora biti poznat,
- s kim se treba umrežiti,
- kakve poslove treba sklapati i kakve firme otvarati,
- koga treba konzultirati.

Pritom nikada nije imao jasnu viziju u stilu „do tridesete želim postići to i to“. Umjesto toga **stalno je imao novi cilj**: titulu, klijenta ili financijski iznos. Kada bi ostvario jedan, mir bi trajao **„dva dana“**, a onda bi uslijedilo pitanje što je sljedeće.

Taj se obrazac, priznaje, prelio iz poslovnog u privatni život. **Cijeli mu je identitet pao pod utjecaj posla**, pa je svoju vrijednost počeo mjeriti isključivo time koliko poslovno vrijedi.
sections.subtitle_en: Goal After Goal: When Work Swallows the Entire Identity
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mislav explains how his identity became tied to work
sections.content_en:
Marko then asks whether they had expectations about what they had to achieve by thirty. Fran jokes that he and Marko are still far from that age because he is 25 years old. Mislav, on the other hand, describes the moment when he entered the **marketing industry**. That was the first time he felt that his success was directly tied to money.

From then on began a series of questions that constantly accompanied him:
- how capable he must be,
- how well-known and to whom he must be known,
- with whom he needs to network,
- what kind of deals he needs to close and what kind of companies to open,
- whom he needs to consult.

At the same time, he never had a clear vision in the style of "by thirty I want to achieve this and that." Instead **he constantly had a new goal**: a title, a client, or a financial amount. When he would achieve one, peace would last for **"two days,"** and then would follow the question of what is next.

That pattern, he admits, spilled over from business into private life. **His entire identity fell under the influence of work**, so he began measuring his worth exclusively by how much he is worth in business.

sections.subtitle: Fran: san o obitelji važniji od diplome
sections.screenshot_description: Fran govori o snu da postane otac i prenese djetetu ono što je naučio od svog oca
sections.content:
Marko se osvrće na pritisak kojemu su mladi izloženi: prije braka moraju imati kuću i sve isplanirano. Podsjeća da su roditelji često pričali kako su počinjali „u sobi“ bez ičega, a s vremenom je na mlade pao teret da sve moraju imati riješeno prije nego što uopće pomisle na brak. U zajednici su, dodaje, mlade upravo zato poticali da ne čekaju.

Fran tada shvaća da je ranije izostavio ono najvažnije. **Od malena mu je cilj bio imati obitelj, biti tata i imati dobru ženu.** Plan mu je bio oženiti se do 27. godine, a to je ostvario tri godine ranije. Iskreno priznaje da je očekivao kako će tijekom studija pronaći suprugu. To mu je uspjelo, ali fakultet nije završio. **Sada čeka dijete, a diploma još nije stigla.** Zato kaže da „po tom pitanju nije previše ambiciozan“.

Očinstvo opisuje kao **svoj životni san**. Želi djetetu prenijeti sve što je naučio od oca i pokazati mu da život nije samo crn, siv ili bijeo, nego da u njemu ima i boje. To smatra svojim **glavnim ostvarenim uspjehom**. Do tridesete bi volio imati kuću i dvorište, a prije svega lijep život: da sa 60 godina može reći da je u mladosti bio pun života, radosti i sreće. Za poslovni dio kaže: „Kako bude, bit će.“

Mislav na to primjećuje da je Fran po tom pitanju **deset godina ispred njega**. Njemu se, kaže, sve dogodilo „ubrzano kroz poslovni segment“, a tek je u tridesetima shvatio što mu je doista važno. Pita se i gdje je bila ovakva zajednica u njegovim dvadesetima. Ipak vjeruje da svi prije ili kasnije, neki i na samrtnoj postelji, dođu do zaključka što je u životu stvarno vrijedno. Egzistencija mora postojati i svijet će uvijek nekoga proglašavati uspješnim ili neuspješnim, ali na kraju, zaključuje Mislav, **„samo nam Bog može reći jesmo li dobri i jesmo li uspješni“**.
sections.subtitle_en: Fran: A Dream of a Family More Important Than a Degree
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran talks about the dream of becoming a father and passing on to his child what he learned from his father
sections.content_en:
Marko reflects on the pressure to which young people are exposed: before marriage they must have a house and everything planned out. He recalls that parents often spoke about how they started out "in a room" without anything, and over time the burden fell on young people that they must have everything solved before they even think about marriage. In the community, he adds, it was precisely for that reason that they encouraged young people not to wait.

Fran then realizes that earlier he had left out the most important thing. **From childhood his goal was to have a family, to be a dad, and to have a good wife.** His plan was to get married by age 27, and he achieved that three years earlier. He honestly admits that he expected to find a wife during his studies. He succeeded in that, but he did not finish college. **Now he is expecting a child, and the degree has not arrived yet.** That is why he says that "regarding that matter he is not overly ambitious."

He describes fatherhood as **his life's dream**. He wants to pass on to his child everything he learned from his father and show him that life is not only black, grey, or white, but that there is also color in it. He considers that his **main accomplished success**. By thirty he would like to have a house and a yard, and above all a nice life: so that at 60 years old he can say that in his youth he was full of life, joy, and happiness. Regarding the business part, he says: "However it will be, it will be."

Mislav observes in response that Fran is **ten years ahead of him** regarding that matter. For him, he says, everything happened "in an accelerated way through the business segment," and only in his thirties did he realize what is truly important to him. He also wonders where such a community was in his twenties. Still, he believes that everyone sooner or later, some even on their deathbed, reaches the conclusion of what is really valuable in life. Sustenance must exist and the world will always proclaim someone successful or unsuccessful, but in the end, Mislav concludes, **"only God can tell us whether we are good and whether we are successful."**

sections.subtitle: Zamka uspoređivanja sa starijima: kad tuđih 35 želiš već s 25
sections.screenshot_description: Fran govori o pritisku kupnje zemljišta i gradnje kuće u 25. godini
sections.content:
Marko priznaje da danas na sve gleda drugačije, i zbog životne dobi. Prepričava razgovor s prijateljem koji mu je rekao da se ne žali jer bi mnogi htjeli biti na njegovu mjestu. Marko mu je odgovorio da je zapravo prijatelj u boljoj poziciji: **mlađi je od njega jedanaest godina, a već ima riješeno ono što se Marku tek sada slaže.** Marko je u toj dobi živio od studentske stipendije.

Priznaje i da se u mlađim danima često uspoređivao sa starijima. Nije to bila ljubomora, nego nestrpljenje: **„Ja to već sad želim.“** Pitao se kada će njemu sve biti posloženo, dok gleda druge kako rješavaju kuće i životne planove. Onda bi zastao i shvatio da ga od tih ljudi dijeli i do 25 godina razlike.

Fran prepoznaje taj obrazac u vlastitom životu. S 25 godina razmišlja o tome kako kupiti zemljište i izgraditi kuću, i to samo zato što pred sobom ima ljude od 33 do 35 godina koji to ostvaruju. Zaboravlja pritom da su oni prošli stvari kroz koje on još nije. U šali spominje kako majci prigovara što nije digla kredit prije dvije godine, kad bi rata bila 200 eura, a sad plaća oko 1000 eura mjesečno.

Zaključak je jasan: to je **nedostatak zdrave ambicije**. Netko blizak, deset godina stariji, postaje mjerilo, a čovjek još nije ni dovoljno odrastao, ni prošao određena iskustva, niti ima dovoljno na računu. **Umjesto manjih, dostižnih ciljeva za iduću godinu, gleda se predaleko u budućnost.**
sections.subtitle_en: The Trap of Comparison with Elders: When You Want Someone Else's 35 Already at 25
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran talks about the pressure of buying land and building a house at age 25
sections.content_en:
Marko admits that today he looks at everything differently, also because of his age in life. He recounts a conversation with a friend who told him not to complain because many would want to be in his place. Marko replied to him that the friend is actually in a better position: **he is eleven years younger than him, and already has solved what is only now coming together for Marko.** Marko lived on a student stipend at that age.

He also admits that in younger days he often compared himself with older people. It wasn't jealousy, but impatience: **"I want that already right now."** He wondered when everything would be arranged for him, while watching others solve houses and life plans. Then he would stop and realize that up to 25 years of age difference separated him from those people.

Fran recognizes that pattern in his own life. At 25 years old he thinks about how to buy land and build a house, and that only because before him he has people 33 to 35 years old who are achieving that. He forgets in doing so that they went through things that he hasn't yet. In jest, he mentions how he complains to his mother that she didn't take out a loan two years ago, when the installment would have been 200 euros, and now she pays around 1000 euros a month.

The conclusion is clear: that is **a lack of healthy ambition**. Someone close, ten years older, becomes the yardstick, while a person is not yet grown up enough, nor has gone through certain experiences, nor has enough in the bank account. **Instead of smaller, attainable goals for the coming year, one looks too far into the future.**

sections.subtitle: Bez usporedbe s drugima, ali najstroži sudac samome sebi
sections.screenshot_description: Mislav objašnjava kako je postao najveći kritičar samome sebi
sections.content:
Marko pita Mislava je li i on, okružen ljudima iz posla, osjećao istu čežnju i potrebu za uspoređivanjem. Usput se šali da njihova zajednica „nije sekta“. Mislav odgovara da je uvijek bio onaj koji **nije htio biti isti kao drugi**. Mreža kontakata bila mu je sastavljena uglavnom od poslovnih ljudi, direktora i članova uprava, ali **nikada nije osjećao potrebu da se s njima uspoređuje**, jer je sve želio napraviti na svoj način.

Majka mu, kaže, često ponavlja da je „sve morao probati“ i svaku grešku napraviti sam. Mislav to prihvaća kao svoj put. Iskustvo ga je naučilo da **dva ista cilja nemaju nužno i dva ista puta**, jer svatko kreće s drukčije početne točke. Odbacuje frazu kako „svi imamo isto 24 sata“. Kao primjer navodi upravo njih trojicu: sva trojica očekuju djecu, dok netko drugi kod kuće „nema ni kučeta ni mačeta“ i brine samo o sebi, a netko ima bolju ili lošiju pozadinu.

Zatim dolazi paradoks. Savjet „gledaj samo sebe“ njemu je istodobno **štetio**, jer je postao **najveći kritičar samome sebi**. Ništa što je napravio nije mu bilo dovoljno dobro. Zaradio bi tisuću, deset tisuća ili sto tisuća eura i opet čuo vlastiti glas: „Mogao si više, mogao si bolje, koji je sljedeći cilj?“ Preispitivao je i svaku kupnju: zašto auto baš sad, zašto ta kuća, zašto nije pričekao. Dodaje da je sa suprugom deset godina i da je u braku „sve super“.
sections.subtitle_en: Without Comparison to Others, but the Harshest Judge to Oneself
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mislav explains how he became the greatest critic to himself
sections.content_en:
Marko asks Mislav whether he too, surrounded by people from business, felt the same longing and need for comparison. In passing, he jokes that their community "is not a sect." Mislav replies that he was always one who **did not want to be the same as others**. His network of contacts was composed mostly of business people, directors, and board members, but **he never felt the need to compare himself with them**, because he wanted to do everything in his own way.

His mother, he says, often repeats to him that he "had to try everything" and make every mistake himself. Mislav accepts that as his path. Experience taught him that **two identical goals do not necessarily have two identical paths**, because everyone starts from a different starting point. He rejects the phrase that "we all have the same 24 hours." As an example he cites precisely the three of them: all three are expecting children, while someone else at home "has neither dog nor cat" and cares only about himself, and someone has a better or worse background.

Then comes the paradox. The advice "look only at yourself" at the same time **harmed** him, because he became **the greatest critic to himself**. Nothing that he did was good enough for him. He would earn a thousand, ten thousand, or a hundred thousand euros and again hear his own voice: "You could have done more, you could have done better, what is the next goal?" He also questioned every purchase: why the car right now, why that house, why didn't he wait. He adds that he has been with his wife for ten years and that in marriage "everything is great."

sections.subtitle: Bi li ranija spoznaja promijenila put? Svatko ima svoj put
sections.screenshot_description: Mislav govori o tome da svaki korak vodi do današnjeg mjesta
sections.content:
Marko pita bi li Mislav radio isto što danas da je pravu životnu vrijednost otkrio deset godina ranije, bez iskustva koje je u međuvremenu stekao. Mislav odlučno odgovara da **sigurno ne bi**. Zato, kaže, ne bi ništa nužno ni mijenjao. Ipak priznaje: što više osvještava prave vrijednosti, to se više pita zašto je sve to uopće radio.

Naglašava i da **svaki prethodni korak vodi do sadašnjeg mjesta**. Sva trojica sada čekaju da im se rode djeca, a ne bi bili tu da ih njihovi postupci nisu doveli do toga. Svatko je imao drukčiju polaznu točku: Marko je od četvrtog razreda znao što želi, Fran je gledao Petrokemiju, a Mislav je imao „svoje brije i svoje probleme“. Na kraju su ipak svi na istom mjestu i razgovaraju o istoj temi jer im je važna. Spominjanje Petrokemije izaziva i šalu: Marko traži da se prikaže njezin logo, a Fran dodaje: „Please sponsor us.“

Marko se slaže da je teško staviti jedan princip na sve i reći da vrijedi za svakoga. Kao primjer navodi vlastitu promjenu mišljenja. Nekada je bio siguran da nikad neće otići iz grada, a danas mu se sviđaju selo i šuma, dok mu stan više nije san. **Prioriteti se mijenjaju**, kaže, zato ne voli isključivost. Svi možda idu prema istom cilju, ali putevi ne moraju izgledati jednako.
sections.subtitle_en: Would Earlier Knowledge Have Changed the Path? Everyone Has Their Own Path
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mislav talks about how every step leads to today's place
sections.content_en:
Marko asks whether Mislav would do the same thing today if he had discovered true life value ten years earlier, without the experience he gained in the meantime. Mislav decisively answers that **he certainly would not**. That is why, he says, he wouldn't necessarily change anything either. Still, he admits: the more he becomes aware of true values, the more he asks himself why he did all of that in the first place.

He also emphasizes that **every previous step leads to the present place**. All three of them are now waiting for their children to be born, and they would not be here if their actions had not led them to that. Everyone had a different starting point: Marko knew what he wanted from the fourth grade, Fran watched Petrokemija, and Mislav had "his own trips and his own problems." In the end, however, they are all in the same place and talking about the same topic because it is important to them. Mentioning Petrokemija also prompts a joke: Marko asks for its logo to be shown, and Fran adds: "Please sponsor us."

Marko agrees that it is difficult to put one principle on everyone and say that it applies to each person. As an example he cites his own change of mind. Once he was sure that he would never leave the city, and today he likes the village and the forest, while an apartment is no longer his dream. **Priorities change**, he says, which is why he does not like exclusivity. Everyone may be heading toward the same goal, but the paths do not have to look the same.

sections.subtitle: Učiti iz tuđih ili iz vlastitih grešaka – sagnuti se ili zaobići
sections.screenshot_description: Marko i Mislav raspravljaju o učenju iz tuđih i vlastitih pogrešaka
sections.content:
Iz razgovora o različitim putevima prirodno se otvara pitanje treba li učiti iz tuđih grešaka. Marko to vidi kroz slikovitu usporedbu. Netko je prevalio **400 kilometara**, uzeo sve što treba i donio ti, pa zašto bi isto vrijeme trošio i sam? Odmah ipak dodaje da nitko nije isti i da bi možda on na istom putu vidio nešto drugo.

Fran se priklanja ideji vlastitog iskustva. Majka ga je uvijek uspoređivala sa starijom sestrom i njezinim učenjem. Odgovarao bi joj da on nije takav: ne voli sjediti nad knjigom, past će ispit i 18 puta, ali proći će ga na svoj način. Slaže se da treba učiti iz tuđih primjera, ali smatra da **nikada ne znamo dok nešto ne iskusimo na vlastitoj koži**.

Mislav dodaje da se životno iskustvo, o kojem govore stariji, ne stječe slušanjem tuđih priča. Taj put, kaže, moraš proći sam. Marko ipak ostaje pri praktičnom pristupu: ako mu netko kaže „pazi, tu sam se lupio u glavu, sagni se“, poslušat će. Mislav na to duhovito odgovara da je njegova varijanta drukčija: **„Možda se ne moram sagnuti, možda mogu zaobići“**, ili preskočiti. Marko zaključuje da je poanta znati da tamo nešto stoji, a kako će netko prijeći preko toga, njegova je stvar.
sections.subtitle_en: Learning from Others' or from One's Own Mistakes – Ducking Down or Going Around
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko and Mislav discuss learning from others' and one's own mistakes
sections.content_en:
From the conversation about different paths naturally opens the question of whether one should learn from others' mistakes. Marko sees that through a vivid comparison. Someone traveled **400 kilometers**, took everything needed, and brought it to you, so why would you spend the same time yourself? Immediately, however, he adds that nobody is the same and that perhaps on the same road he would see something else.

Fran leans toward the idea of one's own experience. His mother always compared him with his older sister and her studying. He would reply to her that he is not like that: he doesn't like sitting over a book, he will fail an exam 18 times, but he will pass it in his own way. He agrees that one should learn from others' examples, but believes that **we never know until we experience something on our own skin**.

Mislav adds that life experience, of which elders speak, is not gained by listening to others' stories. That path, he says, you have to walk yourself. Marko nevertheless sticks to a practical approach: if someone tells him "watch out, I hit my head here, duck down," he will listen. Mislav humorously replies to that that his variant is different: **"Maybe I don't have to duck down, maybe I can go around,"** or jump over. Marko concludes that the point is to know that something stands there, and how someone will cross over that is their own business.

sections.subtitle: „Svi novci ovog svijeta nisu dovoljni ako mi nismo okej“
sections.screenshot_description: Mislav prepričava rečenicu supruge koja mu je bila wake-up call
sections.content:
Marko otvara osjetljivu temu novca. Pita Mislava koliko je svoju uspješnost kao muškarca vezao uz količinu novca koju zarađuje. Dodaje da sumnja kako je itko „cijepljen“ protiv tog osjećaja. Mislav se vraća na survival mod: **„Koliko para dolazi, toliko ti stešaš.“** Njegov stil života nikada nije bio da sa 100.000 eura kupi auto od 100.000 eura. Novac je bio „u vreći, u čarapi“, kao sigurnost koja mu jamči da će sve biti u redu.

Prekretnica je došla s jednom rečenicom njegove supruge: **„Svi novci ovog svijeta nam nisu dovoljni ako mi nismo okej.“** Za Mislava je to bio pravi **wake-up call**. Počeo se pitati za koga i zašto sve to radi. Novac nije rasipao, nego ga je pametno ulagao, ali obitelj nije živjela ništa drukčije nego što bi živjela s možda deset puta manje.
sections.subtitle_en: "All the Money in This World Is Not Enough If We Are Not Okay"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mislav recounts a sentence from his wife that was a wake-up call for him
sections.content_en:
Marko opens the sensitive topic of money. He asks Mislav how much he tied his success as a man to the amount of money he earns. He adds that he doubts that anyone is "vaccinated" against that feeling. Mislav returns to survival mode: **"As much money comes in, that much you stash away."** His lifestyle was never to buy a 100,000-euro car with 100,000 euros. Money was "in a bag, in a sock," as a security that guarantees him that everything will be fine.

The turning point came with one sentence from his wife: **"All the money in this world is not enough for us if we are not okay."** For Mislav, that was a real **wake-up call**. He began asking himself for whom and why he is doing all of that. He did not squander money, but rather invested it smartly, but the family lived no differently than it would have lived with perhaps ten times less.

sections.subtitle: Rođenje kćeri i rez od 70 posto prihoda
sections.screenshot_description: Mislav objašnjava odluku da zbog obitelji smanji 70% prihoda
sections.content:
Suprugine riječi poklopile su se s **rođenjem kćeri**, kada je Mislav donio veliku odluku. Ono što inače radi za poslovne klijente, a to su strukture, procjene rizika i poslovni planovi, primijenio je na vlastiti život. Sve je stavio u tablice, strategiju i korake te **srezao 70 posto svih prihoda**. Kako kaže, to je **70 posto vremena koje mora dobiti za suprugu i kćer**, jer želi biti najbolji tata i najbolji suprug, a stari način života „više ne vodi nigdje“.

Pojašnjava da novcem nikada nije htio nikome ništa dokazati niti se praviti važan u Ferrariju. Svoju je vrijednost mjerio time koliko može uštedjeti i zaraditi da obitelj bude sigurna. Kada je shvatio da im to ništa ne znači, jer **„očito nismo bili dobro, a bilo je para“**, uvidio je da proživljava probleme svoje prve, primarne obitelji i ponavlja njezine obrasce. Njegova primarna obitelj danas je ona koju čini sa suprugom i djetetom, i oni taj scenarij ne moraju živjeti.

Izračunao je koliko im je potrebno za život i za ulaganje u imanje koje obnavljaju te napravio životni i poslovni zaokret. Ispostavilo se nešto iznenađujuće: **cijelo je vrijeme mogao raditi 70 posto manje i imati iste prihode.** „Vratili smo se na stari put, samo smo pametnije odlučili raditi“, kaže Mislav.
sections.subtitle_en: Birth of a Daughter and a 70 Percent Cut in Income
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mislav explains the decision to reduce income by 70% for the sake of the family
sections.content_en:
His wife's words coincided with the **birth of his daughter**, when Mislav made a big decision. What he otherwise does for business clients, which are structures, risk assessments, and business plans, he applied to his own life. He put everything into spreadsheets, strategy, and steps, and **cut 70 percent of all income**. As he says, that is **70 percent of time that he must get for his wife and daughter**, because he wants to be the best dad and the best husband, and the old way of life "leads nowhere anymore."

He explains that with money he never wanted to prove anything to anyone or show off in a Ferrari. He measured his worth by how much he can save and earn so that the family would be safe. When he realized that meant nothing to them, because **"obviously we weren't well, and there was money,"** he saw that he was reliving the problems of his first, primary family and repeating its patterns. His primary family today is the one he forms with his wife and child, and they do not have to live that scenario.

He calculated how much is necessary for them to live and to invest in the estate they are renovating and made a life and business pivot. Something surprising turned out: **all along he was able to work 70 percent less and have the same income.** "We returned to the old path, only we decided to work smarter," says Mislav.

sections.subtitle: Ne služiti Bogu i bogatstvu: vrijednost izvan dobivenih i izgubljenih projekata
sections.screenshot_description: Mislav govori o vjeri kao mjerilu vrijednosti umjesto zarade
sections.content:
Mislav naglašava da mu ni ta promjena nije davala vrijednost. Vodi ga vjera, i to poznata misao da **čovjek ne može služiti Bogu i bogatstvu**. „Moje bogatstvo u mom srcu je Bog i vjera, sve ovo ostalo služi meni“, kaže. Pravilo mu je jednostavno: **ako on počne služiti onome što radi, umjesto da to služi njemu, takvo se što „reže instant“ iz života.**

To nastoji osvještavati svakodnevno, **kroz molitvu i pokušaj da se duhovno i objektivno sagleda izvana**. Upozorava da je lako vratiti se starim obrascima jer suvremeno doba, preko društvenih mreža, televizije i vijesti, uči ljude da štuju ono što bi im trebalo služiti.

Priznaje i što mu se zapravo događalo prije povratka vjeri. **Svaki dobiveni projekt govorio mu je „vrijedan si“, a svaki izgubljeni „nisi vrijedan, moraš ponovno zaslužiti poštovanje prema sebi“.** To je, kaže, bio „krivi pattern cijelo vrijeme“, a riješio ga je, hvala Bogu, njegov povratak vjeri.
sections.subtitle_en: Not Serving God and Wealth: Worth Outside of Won and Lost Projects
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mislav speaks about faith as a measure of worth instead of earnings
sections.content_en:
Mislav emphasizes that even that change did not give him worth. He is guided by faith, and that the well-known thought that **man cannot serve God and wealth**. "My wealth in my heart is God and faith, all the rest of this serves me," he says. His rule is simple: **if he begins serving what he does, instead of it serving him, such a thing is "cut instantly" from life.**

He strives to become aware of this daily, **through prayer and an attempt to view himself spiritually and objectively from the outside**. He warns that it is easy to return to old patterns because the modern era, through social media, television, and news, teaches people to worship what should serve them.

He also admits what was actually happening to him before returning to the faith. **Every won project told him "you are worthy," and every lost one "you are not worthy, you have to earn respect for yourself again."** That, he says, was "the wrong pattern the entire time," and it was resolved, thank God, by his return to the faith.

sections.subtitle: Socijalistički odgoj i bunt protiv riječi „moraš“
sections.screenshot_description: Mislav opisuje socijalistički odgoj i vlastiti bunt protiv tog obrasca
sections.content:
Marko pita dolazi li taj obrazac vrednovanja sebe kroz uspjeh iz obitelji. Mislav odgovara da ne nužno, iako se to uvijek naglašavalo. Njegova je obitelj živjela vjeru, dok je on tada nije živio na isti način. Bez obzira na to, odgajani su, kako on to voli reći, **„socijalistički“**: zaposli se, cijeli život budi u jednoj firmi i u kancelariji, primaj plaću i bit će ti dobro, budi dobar radnik i slušaj što ti se govori.

Protiv toga se Mislav pobunio. „Neće meni nitko govoriti što ja moram“, govorio je, jer za njega **„moraš“ ne postoji**. Ironija je u tome što je taj pritisak onda počeo nametati sam sebi i, kako zaključuje, **„sam sebi postao najveći neprijatelj“**.

Ozbiljnu temu Fran prekida šalom vraćajući se na Petrokemiju. Nudi Mislavu da mu „sredi“ umjetno gnojivo za imanje i dodaje: „Evo, postat ću uspješan.“
sections.subtitle_en: Socialist Upbringing and Rebellion Against the Word "Must"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mislav describes a socialist upbringing and his own rebellion against that pattern
sections.content_en:
Marko asks whether that pattern of evaluating oneself through success comes from the family. Mislav answers not necessarily, although it was always emphasized. His family lived the faith, while he at that time did not live it in the same way. Regardless of that, they were brought up, as he likes to put it, **"socialistically"**: get a job, be in one company and in an office your whole life, receive a salary and you will be fine, be a good worker and listen to what you are told.

Against that Mislav rebelled. "Nobody is going to tell me what I must do," he would say, because for him **"must" does not exist**. The irony is in the fact that he then began imposing that pressure on himself and, as he concludes, **"became the greatest enemy to himself."**

Fran interrupts the serious topic with a joke returning to Petrokemija. He offers to Mislav to "arrange" artificial fertilizer for his estate and adds: "Here, I will become successful."
